summary: Phase 149O.20L.7M -- Dell Redeployment + DeploymentBinding First-Use Sequencing Architecture. FINAL VERDICT: SEQUENCING ARCHITECTURE DEFINED -- READY FOR PROPOSITION PREPARATION. Architecture/design-only phase; no execution of any kind. Derived the exact current deployment candidate SHA (b0840e96a7ffb12308e95828aa5927c3e7c770c0, identical to HEAD/origin/main, confirmed zero later authority-bearing drift beyond 149O.20L.7L.6) rather than assuming HEAD. Confirmed candidate contract versions (HBDC-001 v1.1, HMIC-001 v1.4), implementation_scope_digest (65ff8ab0... recomputed live), the 30-member frozen authority-bearing file set, and the candidate tree inventory (4200 tracked blobs: 4186x100644, 14x100755, zero symlinks/submodules). Reconfirmed the old Dell deployment state (28bf137b..., 4108 blobs) from canonical prior evidence without fresh Dell access. Classified the exact old-Dell-to-candidate diff across exactly five authority-relevant files (no producer -> producer implementation; HBDC v1.0->v1.1; HMIC v1.3->v1.4; 28->30-member frozen scope; contract-text repairs) -- explicitly not collapsed into a generic 'source update.' Determined no venv reinstall is required (confirmed editable install, single unchanged dependency jsonschema) and the launch wrapper is structurally unmutatable by a source-tree checkout swap (lives outside the git-tracked tree at /opt/pcae/runtime/bin/pcae-launch; digest b3e969... unaffected). Analyzed producer-target availability from source: an exact, Dell-bound DeploymentBinding preview requires both the producer deployed on Dell and a RepositoryIdentity already existing there, since the admin module strictly requires an existing RepositoryIdentity (RepositoryIdentityMissingError) and never calls ensure_repository_identity() itself. Reconstructed the RepositoryIdentity creation path (ensure_repository_identity(), UUID4-random, atomic write, fails closed on malformed, idempotent, git-ignored) and confirmed source redeployment does not itself create a RepositoryIdentity. Classified RepositoryIdentity creation as requiring no election (HATP-REQ-048, not named in CHGR condition 6's exclusion list) -- derived from primary source, not inferred from condition 6's silence. Read chgr-0e37ed1340b14311826722c4dbf3e856 directly: condition 6 is an exhaustive six-category exclusion list requiring a fresh, separate election for DeploymentBinding (RepositoryIdentity not named); condition 7 scopes the CHGR's authorization to exactly source SHA 28bf137b..., 'no other source SHA, branch, or ref' -- confirming a fresh CHGR is required for the candidate transition. Independently found and confirmed a fourth, previously-uncounted, git-tracked CHGR (chgr-d4343fa51b9743f3abaeb87a881a78b1, Boundary-P provisioning, plan/commit-bound to an unrelated earlier commit and earlier HMIC/HBDC version pair) is equally inapplicable -- four CHGRs exist in total, none authorizes the candidate transition or first-use action. Fully specified and compared Model A (redeploy-first), Model B (SHA-bound combined proposition), and Model C (two-CHGR sequence) against authority separation, preview fidelity, rollback isolation, failure containment, source-currentness, producer availability, and audit clarity. Determined Models A and C collapse into the same practical sequence (named the 'two-transition model' going forward) because any DeploymentBinding-authorizing election under condition 6 must itself be a fresh CHGR. Rejected Model B on a factual, not preferential, ground: ensure_repository_identity() generates a random UUID4 with no override parameter and no persist-free preview mode, so an exact repository_id -- and therefore an exact DeploymentBinding preview -- cannot exist before a RepositoryIdentity is created, which cannot happen before the producer is deployed on Dell; a genuinely combined, single, pre-election proposition cannot carry exact binding content, making Model B's own core premise factually false (the 'Repository ID preview problem'). Analyzed Model B's rollback complexity (a source-only rollback after identity/binding creation leaves a binding created under newer semantics than the reverted source) as a Model-B-specific hazard absent under the two-transition model. Selected the two-transition model with evidence-based rationale (not phase-count preference). Defined the exact 11-step future governed phase decomposition: source-redeployment proposition-preparation -> independent authority verification -> election+CHGR -> execution -> independent real-host verification, then first-use identity/binding proposition-preparation (RepositoryIdentity created as an unelected administrative step once source is deployed, enabling an exact binding preview) -> independent authority verification -> election+CHGR -> execution+HBDC-readjudication -> independent real-host verification -> Boundary-C preparation. Carried forward, unrepaired, all four named findings (first-use audit-failure-after-mutation gap, permissive timestamp-parser gap, HMIC-REQ-103 revocation-validation gap, HMIC-REQ-063 executed-byte-provenance limitation) with their exact consequence for first-use sequencing derived and documented. Resolved the RepositoryIdentity-determinism, DeploymentBinding-preview-input, timestamp-preview, and signer/provider/scope-resolution questions from primary source, inventing no values. Confirmed D3-3's CLOSED-FOR-CURRENT-CONTINUATION status carries unchanged. No Dell access. No RepositoryIdentity, no DeploymentBinding, no election, no CHGR, no certification, no activation. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable. Recommended next phase: 149O.20L.7N -- Dell Current-Source Redeployment Proposition + Authority Preparation (proposition preparation only; no election in that phase either).
